title: Gut Clostridium aminophilum as a protective microbe in never-smoker lung cancer: insights from metagenomics and machine learning
summary: The model prioritized Clostridium aminophilum as depleted in the LCINS cohort and as a candidate protective microbe; the paper reports supporting cell and mouse tumor-suppression experiments. Held-out test AUC 0.886 (mean 0.855); reduced abundance replicated in an independent NSCLC cohort (29 controls/27 cases), with in-vitro cell and in-vivo xenograft follow-up. The small cohort and non-LCINS replication limit clinical specificity; causal/organism-specific effects remain unresolved.
ai_technology: glmBoost feature selection plus ridge classification, interpreted with SHAP to prioritize a candidate gut microbe
